# Asking contract

The skills that cite this file, each with the part that it uses:

- `/code-execute-issue`: the For-you block, `## Who does what`, the
  end list, and `## Statement budgets` for its plan and its report.
- `/code-execute-all`: the For-you block and the end list.
- `/code-create-issues`: the For-you block, `## Who does what` and the
  end list, for its Handoff template, and `## Statement budgets`.
- `/code-create-prd`, `/code-publish-pr` and `/code-retro`:
  `## Statement budgets` only.

## Scope

In this part and in the two parts after it, "you" in a block is
jcleira, and argos is the agent. The parts after them speak as jcleira
("I") to the agent ("you").

The files keep their full depth: the PRD, `issues.md`, and the issue
files. Text that reaches jcleira in the chat follows the For-you shape
below and the chat budgets. A stop is text in the chat too. Handoff
blocks have no exemption: a Handoff that reaches jcleira is a For-you
block. Each question follows `## Questions` in `CLAUDE.md`.

## The For-you block

Each ask that reaches jcleira in the chat has one shape:

1. **The header line.** One line: the repo, the slice number and the
   slice title, as `<repo> slice <N>: <title>`. The driver of
   `/code-execute-all` writes it. In a session without the driver, the
   slice writes it.
2. **`## For you`.** Then these four parts, in this order:
   1. **The need.** One sentence of 25 words or less: what argos needs
      from jcleira.
   2. **The body.** One of these:
      - numbered steps, each with the full URL, the action and what
        jcleira will see;
      - one yes-line, with the reason, for a change that argos cannot
        undo, or with the cost, for a paid action that argos can make;
      - the options, with the pick of argos.
   3. **The status line.** What is done, then the words
      `For the full report, reply "report".`
   4. **The last line.** One of these two lines:
      - **`Reply:`** and the exact words, in quotes.
      - **`Check:`** and a command in backticks, when the body is steps
        and a read-only command can see that they are done: a key on
        GitHub, a merged PR, a page that answers. The command exits 0
        when the steps are done, and changes nothing. Argos runs it
        every 15 seconds, up to 60 minutes, and goes on when it passes,
        so jcleira does not reply. The line says so.

      Why: on 2026-10-08 a block asked jcleira to add a key on GitHub,
      and to reply. jcleira answered "do everything yourself please".
      Argos then ran a read-only check every 15 seconds, and the run
      went on one minute later with no reply.
3. **No ask.** `## For you`, then the line `Nothing now.`
4. **`## End list`.** After the block, one item per line. Each item
   starts with one of three labels:
   - `Not checked:` a test that argos cannot run;
   - `Ask:` a need that the next step does not need;
   - `Changed:` an outside change, with an `Undo:` part that tells how
     to undo it.

The block speaks to "you", names a slice by its title, and uses
ASD-STE100. It never holds:

- a field name or a file edit for jcleira;
- a `<placeholder>`;
- a secret;
- a note for the next agent;
- `claude --resume`, or an instruction to run a code-* skill again.

The stop check, `skills/code-execute-issue/stop-check.py`, holds each
block to the ten rules of `/code-execute-issue` (§5 step 8). It does
not check the header line, the status line or the body form. A test
runs it on each example below.

+Add a configurable timeout that wraps the full execution of each Partio git hook (pre-commit, post-commit, pre-push). When a hook times out, it logs a warning with the elapsed time and exits 0 so the git operation is never blocked.

+Source: [entireio/cli#957](https://github.com/entireio/cli/issues/957) — repeated hook timeouts when agent detection or checkpoint operations stall; [entireio/cli#956](https://github.com/entireio/cli/issues/956) — transcript flush sentinel timeout causing token-count failures on slow sessions.
+## What to build
+1. Add a `HookTimeout` field (`Duration`) to `Config` in `internal/config/config.go`.
+2. Set the default to 30 seconds in `internal/config/defaults.go`.
+3. Map the `PARTIO_HOOK_TIMEOUT` environment variable in `internal/config/env.go`, parsing it with `time.ParseDuration`.
+4. In `internal/hooks/runner.go`, derive a `context.WithTimeout` from `cfg.HookTimeout` and thread it into each hook call.

+5. In `runPreCommit`, `runPostCommit`, and `runPrePush` (or in the `Runner` methods), select on the context deadline: when the context is cancelled due to timeout, log a warning that names the hook and the elapsed time, and return nil (exit 0). The warning also names the step that was running when the timeout fired (use the step names of #48). #398 (closed) asked for this.
+6. Add unit tests in `internal/hooks/` that inject a mock operation exceeding the timeout and assert: the hook returns nil, and a warning is logged.

+The timeout applies to the full hook body, not just initialization. #343 (a start-up timeout) is closed: that hang is in the macOS loader, before `main`, so only the hook script can bound it (`internal/git/hooks/hooks.go`).

+**Stop the git children (from #418).** Today each git subprocess starts with `exec.Command` and no context: `execGit` (`internal/git/git.go:17`), `internal/git/repo.go:25`, `internal/checkpoint/store.go:40`, `:57` and `:181`. `CommandContext` occurs nowhere. So when the hook returns at the deadline, the running git child is not stopped, and it goes on after the hook exits. Pass the hook context down and start these calls with `exec.CommandContext(ctx, …)`, so that the deadline kills the child.

+- [ ] `Config` has a `HookTimeout Duration` field that serialises to JSON
+- [ ] The default value is 30 seconds
+- [ ] Setting `PARTIO_HOOK_TIMEOUT=10s` overrides the default
+- [ ] The same value can be set in any layer of the config hierarchy (global, repo, local)
+- [ ] When pre-commit, post-commit, or pre-push exceeds the timeout, the hook exits 0 and logs a warning with the hook name, the elapsed time and the step that was running
+- [ ] Normal hook execution (under the timeout) is unaffected
+- [ ] Unit tests cover the timeout path using a mock long-running operation
+- [ ] At the deadline, a git subprocess that is still running is killed (`exec.CommandContext`), not left running after the hook exits

+## Summary

+`partio enable` already warns about Husky, Lefthook and Overcommit (`warnHookManagers` in `cmd/partio/enable.go`, backed by `DetectHookManagers` in `internal/git/hooks/detect_hook_managers.go`). Two gaps stay: `partio doctor` does not report hook managers, and no command warns when `core.hooksPath` is set.
+## Problem

+Partio installs its hooks in `<git common dir>/hooks`: `git.HooksDir` (`internal/git/repo.go`) uses `git rev-parse --git-common-dir`, and the hook scripts use the same path. When `core.hooksPath` is set, git runs the hooks from that path only. Partio's hooks then never run, and no commit gets a checkpoint. `partio doctor` checks the same directory, so it still reports `[OK]` for each hook.
+## Desired Behavior
+- `partio doctor` lists the hook managers that `DetectHookManagers` finds, with the same instructions as `partio enable`
+- `partio enable` and `partio doctor` warn when `core.hooksPath` points to a directory other than the one Partio installs into
+- `partio doctor` does not report `[OK]` for a hook that git does not run
+- Detection is informational only: it does not block installation
+## Source
+Inspired by entireio/cli#1137
+## Acceptance Criteria
+- [ ] `partio doctor` reports Husky, Lefthook and Overcommit when `DetectHookManagers` detects them
+- [ ] With `core.hooksPath` set to another directory, `partio enable` prints a warning that names the path, and `partio doctor` reports `[WARN]` for each Partio hook and counts it as an issue
+- [ ] Without `core.hooksPath`, the output of both commands does not change
+- [ ] Detection does not block `partio enable`
+Proposal id: detect-conflicting-hook-managers
+## Description

+Add a `--json` flag to `partio rewind --list`, so that a script or a CI job can read the checkpoint list. The list prints one line per checkpoint today (`cmd/partio/rewind.go`): the checkpoint ID, `branch=`, `agent=` and `created=`.

+The flag uses the same name as `partio status --json` (#220) and `partio explain --json` (#64). The global `--output jsonl` flag of the first version of this issue is out of scope: it would give `partio status` a second flag for the output of #220.
+Inspired by entireio/cli#1192, which added JSONL output modes to `entire review` for programmatic event consumption.
+## What to build
+1. Add a `--json` flag to `partio rewind` in `cmd/partio/rewind.go`. It applies to `--list`, with or without `--branch`.
+2. With `--json`, print one JSON object per checkpoint, one object per line, to stdout: `id`, `branch`, `agent_percent`, `created_at`. Print no header line.
+3. A checkpoint with unavailable or invalid metadata gives an object with `id` and an `error` field.
+4. With `--json` and no checkpoints, print nothing and exit 0.
+5. Without `--json`, the output does not change.
+## Acceptance Criteria
+- [ ] `partio rewind --list --json` prints one JSON object per checkpoint, one per line, with `id`, `branch`, `agent_percent` and `created_at`
+- [ ] `partio rewind --list --branch <name> --json` prints only the checkpoints of that branch, in the same format
+- [ ] A checkpoint with unreadable metadata gives an object with `id` and `error`, and the list continues
+- [ ] Without `--json`, the output of `partio rewind --list` does not change
+- [ ] Tests cover the JSON output, the branch filter and a checkpoint with invalid metadata
+## Premise
+<!-- partio:premise:v1 -->
+- Partio's CLI commands output only unstructured human-readable text [evidence: `cmd/partio/status.go`]
+- There is no global `--output` flag in the root command [evidence: `cmd/partio/main.go`]
+## Gathered Evidence
+**Claim 1:** Partio's CLI commands output only unstructured human-readable text
+- Evidence: `cmd/partio/status.go`, `cmd/partio/rewind.go`
+- Verdict: holds

+- Excerpt: `status.go` uses `fmt.Printf` for all output (e.g. `fmt.Printf("Repository: %s\n", repoRoot)`). `rewind.go` uses `fmt.Printf`/`fmt.Println` for all output. No JSON, structured, or JSONL output paths exist in either file.
+**Claim 2:** There is no global `--output` flag in the root command
+- Evidence: `cmd/partio/main.go`
+- Verdict: holds
+- Excerpt: `root.PersistentFlags()` in `newRootCmd()` only registers `--log-level`. No `--output` or format flag is defined anywhere in `cmd/partio/`.
+Proposal id: add-jsonl-streaming-output
+## Description

+Add a `partio import` command that discovers pre-existing Claude Code transcripts from `~/.claude/projects/` and retroactively creates checkpoints for them. Users who adopt Partio on an existing repo have session history predating hook installation; this command lets them ingest that history into the checkpoint branch.
+Inspired by entireio/cli#1336 — "Bulk Import existing Claude Code transcripts into Entire to make cold start better."
+## What to build
+Add `cmd/partio/import.go` with a `partio import` Cobra subcommand:
+1. **Discover transcripts**: Walk `~/.claude/projects/<sanitized-repo-path>/` (using the same path sanitization as `internal/agent/claude/find_session_dir.go`) and collect all `*.jsonl` files
+2. **Parse each transcript**: Reuse `internal/agent/claude/parse_jsonl.go` to extract `agent.SessionData` per file

+3. **Correlate to commits**: For each parsed session, attempt to match a historical commit by comparing the session's timestamp window against `git log` timestamps; leave commit hash empty when no confident match is found
+4. **Deduplicate**: Read existing checkpoints from the orphan branch and skip any session whose `SessionID` is already present
+5. **Dry-run support**: With `--dry-run`, print what would be imported without writing anything
+6. **Write checkpoints**: For each non-skipped session, call `checkpoint.Store.Write()` with a `Checkpoint` populated from the session data
+7. **Report**: Print N transcripts found, M imported, K skipped (already present)

+**Notes (argos review, 2026-10-10).** (1) Step 3 matches a session to a commit by time only. A commit without a `Partio-Checkpoint` trailer had no active agent at pre-commit (`internal/hooks/postcommit.go:47-49`), so it is often a human-only commit, and a time match alone repeats the #755 false attribution. Leave the commit hash empty unless the edits of the session match the files of the commit: this is the attribution design call of #342, #372, #396 and #755. (2) Step 2 needs #423 first: today `ParseJSONL` drops typed prompts whose `message.content` is a string, so an imported checkpoint gets an empty or wrong prompt.
+## Acceptance Criteria
+- [ ] `partio import` command is registered in `cmd/partio/main.go`
+- [ ] With no arguments, scans `~/.claude/projects/<current-repo-path>/` for JSONL files
+- [ ] Each discovered JSONL is parsed using `internal/agent/claude/parse_jsonl.go`
+- [ ] Sessions already present in the checkpoint branch (matched by `SessionID`) are skipped
+- [ ] `--dry-run` flag prints what would be imported without writing checkpoints
+- [ ] After import, new checkpoints appear in `partio status`
+- [ ] Running import twice produces the same checkpoints (idempotent)
+- [ ] Summary printed: N found, M imported, K skipped

+- Partio has no existing command for retroactive transcript import [evidence: `cmd/partio/`]
+- Claude Code stores JSONL transcripts under `~/.claude/projects/` [evidence: `internal/agent/claude/find_session_dir.go`]
+- The checkpoint struct stores a `SessionID` field usable for deduplication [evidence: `internal/checkpoint/checkpoint.go`]
+## Gathered Evidence
+**Claim 1**: Partio has no existing command for retroactive transcript import
+- Evidence: `cmd/partio/` directory
+- Verdict: holds

+- Excerpt: cmd/partio/ contains clean.go, cleanup_sessions.go, disable.go, doctor.go, enable.go, explain.go, hook.go, main.go, prune.go, reset.go, resume.go, rewind.go, status.go, version.go — no import.go
+**Claim 2**: Claude Code stores JSONL transcripts under `~/.claude/projects/`
+- Evidence: `internal/agent/claude/find_session_dir.go`
+- Verdict: holds
+- Excerpt: `projectsDir := filepath.Join(home, ".claude", "projects")` (line 24)
+**Claim 3**: The checkpoint struct stores a `SessionID` field usable for deduplication
+- Evidence: `internal/checkpoint/checkpoint.go`
+- Verdict: holds
+- Excerpt: `SessionID string` with json tag "session_id" in Checkpoint struct (line 12)

# The count after the merge

This command counts the copies that get through the search after the
merge of the ranked candidates (user story 32). It lists the proposals
that were filed on or after the merge date and that a person closed by
hand as copies.

## The command

Set `MERGE_DATE` to the day of the merge, as `YYYY-MM-DD`:

```bash
MERGE_DATE=2026-10-16
gh issue list --repo partio-io/cli --label minion-proposal --state closed \
  --search "created:>=$MERGE_DATE" --limit 300 --json number,stateReason,comments \
  --jq '[.[] | select(.stateReason == "DUPLICATE" or any(.comments[]; .body | test("^Duplicate of #"))) | .number] | sort'
```

The command only reads. It needs `gh` with read access to
`partio-io/cli`.

## How to read the output

- The output is a JSON list of issue numbers, sorted. Each number is a
  proposal that a person closed as a copy of an older one.
- A hand close of a copy has the state reason `duplicate`, or a comment
  that starts with `Duplicate of #`. For example, #758 was closed as
  `completed`, with the comment "Duplicate of #710 …".
- The review gate closes with `not_planned` and a comment that starts
  with `<!-- partio:review:v1 -->`. The command does not count these
  closes: the gate stopped those copies.
- `[]` means that no copy got through. Each number in the list is a
  copy that the search did not stop. When the list is not empty, the
  full list of the proposal titles, for a judgment of meaning, is the
  next step (PRD).
- The command reads at most 300 closed proposals. When the window holds
  more, make it shorter.

## The check window

The window before the merge, `created:2026-10-07..2026-10-13`, gives a
known output. Use it to check the command:

```bash
gh issue list --repo partio-io/cli --label minion-proposal --state closed \
  --search "created:2026-10-07..2026-10-13" --limit 300 --json number,stateReason,comments \
  --jq '[.[] | select(.stateReason == "DUPLICATE" or any(.comments[]; .body | test("^Duplicate of #"))) | .number] | sort'
```

Output on 2026-10-16:

```
[757,758,768,771]
```

These are the four copies after #750 that the PRD names.
